data.why: The app ships its own example dataset (v0/data/example.json) and loads it by default on startup via an inlined import in main.js; it's also a valid file for the 'Upload Data > Local' button, so the same file is exposed as an upload sample.

goals: View the default example deep mutational scanning dataset mapped onto its 3D protein structure on load
Brush/select a range of sites in the context plot to zoom the focus plot and see those sites highlighted on the structure
Switch between conditions/epitopes in the legend to compare escape patterns across conditions on the same structure
Change the summary metric (e.g. mean/sum/max escape) and toggle floor/mutation-count display to re-derive site-level values
Upload a different dms-viz-formatted JSON file (local file or remote URL) to visualize a new dataset
Adjust protein/selection/ligand representation, color, and opacity, then download the protein structure image and the plot image

review.summary: The 2-D exploration half of dms-viz is captured well: the brushed overview, site selection, the per-site heatmap, summary metrics and filters, URL state and export, with clean general labels and screens that mostly support them. But the structure never loaded, and the tree quietly leaves out the 3D structure view that the README names as the tool's purpose, so it needs a structure phase and features added (preferably from a re-run with RCSB reachable) before it is filed.
